description: EarthStat serves geographic data sets on how to feed a growing population while reducing agriculture's environmental impact. It is a collaboration between the Global Landscapes Initiative at the University of Minnesota's Institute on the Environment and the Land Use and Global Environment lab at the University of British Columbia. Data sets include global cropland and pasture area circa 2000, built from agricultural inventory data and satellite land cover; harvested area and yield of 175 crops circa 2000 on a five arc-minute grid (about 10 by 10 kilometres), combining national, state and county census statistics with a global cropland map; greenhouse gas emissions and intensity from croplands, including rice paddies, peatland drainage and nitrogen fertiliser; and a new data set on crop allocation to food, feed and non-food uses. Coverage is global. Downloads are free from the site; the licence is not stated on the home page read. Caveats: most layers describe conditions around the year 2000 and have not been updated annually. For simulation it provides gridded crop area and yield for exposure of agriculture to hazards and for food supply and climate scenarios. Related catalogue records include FAOSTAT, FAO GAEZ and the USDA Cropland Data Layer.
